name: Mechanical Engineering

declaration.notes: SEAS first-years declare a major in their second semester (deadline March 1 per the 2026 orientation deck); no course or GPA prerequisites are stated and majors are not capped. College (or other UVA school) students must apply for internal transfer to SEAS: cumulative GPA > 2.0, good standing, and completed APMA 1090|MATH 1310 (Fall 2025+ starters), APMA 1110|MATH 1320, APMA 2120|MATH 2310, CHEM 1410|1610|1810 + lab 1411|1611|1811, CS 1110-1113, PHYS 1420|1425|1710 + lab PHYS 1429|2030; windows Nov 15-Dec 15 (spring entry) and May 1-Jun 1 (fall entry); accepted students are placed in their major of choice (no caps). See TRANSFER.md.

requirements.label: Engineering mathematics
requirements.note: APMA 1090 required beginning with the Class of 2029 curriculum (Fall 2025 entrants); earlier sheets started at APMA 1110. MATH equivalents per the SEAS internal-transfer page (MATH 3250 for APMA 2130 per CE 3100 prerequisite text).

requirements.label: Physics I and II
requirements.note: Physics II may be PHYS 2415 + PHYS 2419 or ECE 2200 (Applied Physics).

requirements.label: Engineering foundations
requirements.note: Rodman Scholars take ENGR 1410/1420. Transfer students may replace ENGR 1020 with 3 other credits by appeal.

requirements.label: Science, Technology and Society
requirements.note: STS 4500 in fall and STS 4600 in spring of fourth year (senior thesis).

requirements.label: Math and science elective
requirements.note: Footnote 2 of the ME sheet: BIOL 2100 or 2200, CHEM 1620, MSE 2090, PHYS 2620, or any APMA 2000+ not required by the major and not duplicating another APMA course. MAE handout also lists CHEM 1420.

requirements.label: Mechanical engineering core
requirements.note: CE 2300/2310 equivalence assumed from cross-listing in prerequisite text (CE 2310 prereq 'CE 2300 or MAE 2300'); confirm with advisor.

requirements.label: Capstone design
requirements.note: Either MAE 4610/4620 or MAE 4690/4700.

requirements.label: Math-science / technical electives
requirements.note: From the MAE Approved Math-Science/Technical Electives list (handout labelled Classes of 2022-2025, the newest found): List 1 math-science (BIOL 2100/2200, CHEM 1420, MSE 2090, PHYS 2620, non-required APMA 2000+); List 2 (ASTR/BIOL/CHEM 2000+, EVSC 2050+, MATH 3300+, PHYS 2620+, STAT 3000+, APMA 3000+, all below 6000); List 3 any SEAS course 3000+ (or a 2000-level SEAS course required for that discipline's major/minor), NASC 3100/3200; no STS or ENGR except one of ENGR 4880 or STS 4810 (Business minor only); no MAE capstone design courses. Only courses on the list count. Courses required by the major cannot double count.

requirements.label: Humanities and social sciences electives
requirements.note: 9 credits from the SEAS approved Humanities and Social Science list (A122 Thornton Hall / SEAS Undergraduate Handbook); not every course qualifies.

requirements.label: Unrestricted electives
requirements.note: Any graded University course except math below MATH 1310 and courses that substantially duplicate degree courses (e.g. PHYS 1010, 1020, 2010, 2020, CS 1010, other intro programming).

notes: Encodes the Class of 2029 ME curriculum sheet (dated 10/29/2025; 131 credits by semester totals). Earlier classes (2025-2028) had a 128-credit sheet without APMA 1090. Credits: MAE 2020 (2), 2040 (1), 2300 (3), 2100 (3), 2310 (3), 2320 (3), 2330 (2), 3210 (3), 3230 (2), 3310 (3), 3710 (3), 3140 (3), 3420 (3), 3620 (3), 3840 (2), 4710 (4), capstone 3+3; APMA 3140 (3), 3110 (3). D is passing but cumulative GPA 2.0 required to graduate. Missing credits (e.g. from AP placement) must be replaced with an additional math/science/technical course at equal or higher level. Only CE 2310 prerequisite text was found for MAE prerequisites (course catalog not readable), so coursePrereqs is sparse. Optional minors (e.g. aerospace) are mentioned on the department page but no ME or aerospace minor is listed on the SEAS Majors and Minors page.

name: Chemical Engineering

declaration.notes: SEAS first-years declare a major in their second semester (deadline March 1 per the 2026 orientation deck); no course or GPA prerequisites are stated and majors are not capped. Core ChE courses require C/CR in their prerequisites (only one passing grade below C allowed among core prerequisites). College (or other UVA school) students must apply for internal transfer to SEAS: cumulative GPA > 2.0, good standing, and completed APMA 1090|MATH 1310 (Fall 2025+ starters), APMA 1110|MATH 1320, APMA 2120|MATH 2310, CHEM 1410|1610|1810 + lab 1411|1611|1811, CS 1110-1113, PHYS 1420|1425|1710 + lab PHYS 1429|2030; windows Nov 15-Dec 15 (spring entry) and May 1-Jun 1 (fall entry); accepted students are placed in their major of choice (no caps). See TRANSFER.md.

requirements.label: Engineering mathematics
requirements.note: APMA 1090 required beginning with the Class of 2029 curriculum (Fall 2025 entrants); earlier sheets started at APMA 1110. MATH equivalents per the SEAS internal-transfer page (MATH 3250 for APMA 2130 per CE 3100 prerequisite text).

requirements.label: Chemistry sequence
requirements.note: 1400 series (AP credit does not waive CHEM 1411/1421) or the all-or-nothing 1800 series plus one selected CHEM course (CHEM 2820, 4090, 4320, 4440, 4410, or another CHEM 4xxx/5xxx with ChE approval). Do not switch sequences mid-program. CHEM 1420 presumably fills the SEAS math & science elective.

requirements.label: Physical chemistry
requirements.note: CHE 4561 topic 'Physical Chemistry for Engineers' (recommended), CHEM 3410, or CHEM 3610.

requirements.label: Physics I and II
requirements.note: Physics II may be PHYS 2415 + PHYS 2419 or ECE 2200 (Applied Physics).

requirements.label: Engineering foundations
requirements.note: Rodman Scholars take ENGR 1410/1420. Transfer students may replace ENGR 1020 with 3 other credits by appeal.

requirements.label: Science, Technology and Society
requirements.note: STS 4500 in fall and STS 4600 in spring of fourth year (senior thesis).

requirements.label: Chemical engineering core
requirements.note: Grade of C or CR expected in core prerequisites; two or more below-C grades in core prerequisites must be retaken. The B.S. page also lists CHE 2246 (Intro to Biotechnology) among core courses, but neither curriculum sheet includes it, so it is not encoded as required.

requirements.label: ChE electives
requirements.note: CHE 4561/4562 special topics need individual approval. The page's footnote list omits CHE 4445, 4452, 4456; confirm with advisor.

requirements.label: ChE or engineering elective
requirements.note: One course with substantial engineering content (approved list in the department office / SIS Academic Requirements); CHE electives also count. Subject ranges are an approximation.

requirements.label: Technical elective
requirements.note: Special topics/projects and courses introduced after 2011-12 need individual approval.

requirements.label: Humanities and social sciences electives
requirements.note: 9 credits from the SEAS approved Humanities and Social Science list (A122 Thornton Hall / SEAS Undergraduate Handbook); not every course qualifies.

requirements.label: Unrestricted electives
requirements.note: Any graded University course except math below MATH 1310 and courses that substantially duplicate degree courses (e.g. PHYS 1010, 1020, 2010, 2020, CS 1010, other intro programming). APMA 1090 does not count as unrestricted if it is counted in the math sequence.

notes: Built from the B.S. page (128-credit minimum, elective lists, sample plan) and the Nov 2023 'broad-based' curriculum sheet; no Class of 2029 ChE sheet was found, so APMA 1090 is included per the SEAS-wide Class of 2029 rule. Corequisites are folded into coursePrereqs (CHE 2202 co-req APMA 2120; CHE 2216 co-req APMA 2130; CHE 3318 co-req CHE 3322; CHE 3398 co-req CHE 3322; CHE 4474/4475 co-reqs of each other). Elective counts (2 ChE, 1 ChE-or-engineering, 1 technical, 3 HSS, 3 unrestricted) come from the B.S. page sample plan, whose listed blocks total only 111 credits; the department also offers data-science and pre-med curriculum variants. The Chemistry Department sets its own minimum grades for CHEM courses.

name: Chemical Engineering

declaration.notes: Contact the ChE undergraduate program coordinator; no eligibility rules stated.

requirements.label: Chemical engineering minor courses
requirements.note: Each course's prerequisites must also be met; students whose major lacks thermodynamics, numerical methods and PDEs may need CHE 2202 and/or CHE 2216 before the 3000-level courses.

notes: Five courses (credits not stated; roughly 17 credits based on the B.S. plan: CHE 2215 3, 3316 4, 3318 3, 3321 3, 3322 4). The C/CR grade rule for core prerequisites applies to the minor too. The page does not say whether non-SEAS students may declare.
